description: The line plot illustrates the performance of two large language models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, measured as Accuracy@1 (%) on the y-axis, against the number of child nodes (tree width) on the x-axis, which ranges from 1 to 7. The y-axis is linear, scaled from 15% to 35%, with major tick marks every 5 percentage points. The GPT-4o model, represented by a solid blue line with circular markers, begins at 24.4% accuracy for 1 child node, rises to 28.9% at 3 nodes, peaks at 34.4% at 5 nodes, and then declines to 31.1% at 7 nodes. The Claude-3.5-Sonnet model, shown as a dashed blue line with 'x' markers, starts at 26.7% for 1 node, increases slightly to 27.8% at 3 nodes, then decreases to 24.4% at 5 nodes, and further drops to 20.0% at 7 nodes. Both models show non-monotonic behavior, with GPT-4o achieving its highest accuracy at a tree width of 5, while Claude-3.5-Sonnet’s performance degrades after an initial slight increase.
